title: Spiritus Invictus: Why Faith Forward Exists
excerpt: Today is All Saints' Day, the day the Church remembers the great cloud of witnesses who ran their race and finished it. It is a fitting day to begin. Saints are not people who never fell. They are people who got back…
description: Faith Forward Foundation launches in St. Louis to serve homeless and displaced veterans, their families, and the dogs who stand beside them.

title: Veterans Day and St. Martin of Tours: The Soldier Who Shared His Cloak
excerpt: November 11 is Veterans Day in the United States. It began as Armistice Day, marking the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month of 1918, when the guns fell silent on the Western Front. It is also, by…
description: On Veterans Day the Church honors St. Martin of Tours, a soldier who cut his cloak in half for a freezing beggar. His example is still our mission.

title: The Dog at His Side: Why Animals Matter in Veteran Homelessness
excerpt: If you ask an outreach worker what keeps veterans on the street, you'll hear the usual list: addiction, untreated trauma, a criminal record, no ID, broken family ties, a benefits claim stuck somewhere in a stack. Ask…
description: Many unhoused veterans have a dog, and many turn down shelter rather than give it up. Here's why Faith Forward built a K9 program around that bond.

title: Gratitude in the Hard Places: A Veteran's Thanksgiving
excerpt: Paul wrote "in every thing give thanks" while living a life of shipwrecks, beatings, prison cells, and hunger. Notice the word: in every thing, not for every thing. Nobody is asked to be thankful for PTSD, for a lost…
description: Thanksgiving can be painful for veterans who are alone or unhoused. How faith teaches gratitude in hard places, and how you can bring a seat to the table.

title: Advent for the Unhoused: Waiting in the Dark for the Light
excerpt: Advent begins today, the first Sunday of a four-week season of preparation for Christmas. The Church lights one candle on the Advent wreath, then two, then three, then four. The light grows slowly, one week at a…
description: Advent is a season of waiting in darkness for light. For veterans waiting on housing, claims, and healing, it carries a message of real hope.

title: Winter Survival: How to Help a Veteran Living Outside This Season
excerpt: St. Louis winters are dangerous for anyone living outside. Wind, wet cold, and sudden freezes can turn a hard night into a deadly one. Hypothermia can set in well above freezing when someone is wet, exhausted, or has…
description: A practical guide to helping veterans survive a St. Louis winter: what to give, what to watch for, and how to connect them to warming centers.

title: Moral Injury: The Wound No One Sees
excerpt: Many veterans carry a wound that is not exactly PTSD. Clinicians and chaplains call it moral injury: the lasting damage that comes from doing, failing to prevent, or witnessing something that violates your deepest…
description: Moral injury is the deep wound of guilt and betrayal that many veterans carry. Faith communities are uniquely placed to help it heal.

title: No Room at the Inn: Christmas and the Homeless Veteran
excerpt: "No room." Two words in the Christmas story that most of us read past. A pregnant young woman and a tired carpenter went door to door in a crowded town and heard the same answer again and again. So the Son of God was…
description: Christ was born to a family with no room at the inn. This Christmas, Faith Forward invites St. Louis to make room for veterans and their families.

title: Starting Over: A New Year Battle Plan for Veterans
excerpt: New Year's resolutions fail because they are wishes, not plans. Veterans know the difference. You never rolled out the gate with a vague hope; you had an operations order. Let's write one for your year.
description: Use military planning skills for a real fresh start in the new year: mission, objectives, resources, and a battle buddy. Faith makes it possible.

title: Meet Gypse: The Blue Nose Pit Bull Leading Our K9 Program
excerpt: Every program needs a first team. Ours is Rev. Mr. Paul Moore and Gypse, a two-year-old female blue nose pit bull with a big heart and a bigger appetite for learning.
description: Meet Gypse, the two-year-old blue nose pit bull and founding dog of the Faith Forward K9 Program, and learn why the founder is training with her first.

title: Understanding PTSD: What Families and Churches Need to Know
excerpt: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) can develop after a person experiences or witnesses a life-threatening or deeply traumatic event. Many veterans live with it, and so do survivors of assault, accidents, and…
keywords: how to help veteran with PTSD
description: A plain-language guide to post-traumatic stress for families and church communities: signs, myths, how to help, and where to find care in St. Louis.

title: Brotherhood After the Uniform: Fighting Isolation
excerpt: In uniform, you were never alone. You ate, slept, trained, and fought next to people who would die for you. Then you got out, and suddenly no one had your back. For many veterans, losing the unit hurts more than…
description: Isolation is one of the most dangerous threats veterans face after service. How to rebuild brotherhood, and why the Church was built for it.

title: Why Counting Matters: The Point-in-Time Count
excerpt: Every January, communities across the U.S. conduct the Point-in-Time (PIT) Count, a one-night snapshot of people experiencing homelessness, both sheltered and unsheltered. Volunteers walk streets, parks, and camps in…
description: Each January communities count people experiencing homelessness. Here's why the Point-in-Time Count matters for veterans and how volunteers can help.

title: Service Dog, ESA, or Pet? A Plain-English Guide to the Law
excerpt: Veterans with dogs are often told different things by different people: "You need a vest." "You need a certificate." "ESAs can go anywhere." Most of it is wrong. Here is a plain-English overview. (This is general…
keywords: service dog vs emotional support animal
description: What's the legal difference between a service dog, an emotional support animal, and a pet? A plain-English guide for veterans on ADA, housing, and travel.

title: Lent for Warriors: Discipline, Sacrifice, and Grace
excerpt: This Wednesday, February 10, the Church begins Lent with ashes and the ancient words: "Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return." For forty days, Christians prepare for Easter through prayer, fasting,…
description: Ash Wednesday opens Lent, a 40-day season of discipline that veterans understand well. A warrior's guide to prayer, fasting, and almsgiving.

title: Love That Stays: Veteran Marriages and Families
excerpt: Valentine's Day is about romance, but the love that holds veteran families together looks less like flowers and more like 1 Corinthians 13: patient, kind, enduring.
description: Deployment, injury, and transition strain veteran marriages. A faith-based look at keeping love strong, plus resources for St. Louis veteran families.

title: The VA Healthcare Maze: A Field Guide for St. Louis
excerpt: For many veterans, the hardest part of VA healthcare is getting in the door. Here is a field guide for the St. Louis area. Systems change, so confirm details when you call.
description: How to enroll in VA healthcare in St. Louis, what to bring, where to go, and how to get help when the system feels impossible.

title: Addiction and Recovery: There Is No Pit So Deep
excerpt: Corrie ten Boom's sister Betsie said it in a Nazi concentration camp: "There is no pit so deep that God's love is not deeper still." Many veterans know the pit of addiction from the inside, and so does our founder.
description: Addiction affects many veterans. A faith-based message of hope for recovery, with practical steps and St. Louis treatment resources.

title: Training the Handler First: Lessons From the K9 Program
excerpt: Military working dog handlers have a saying: "It travels down the leash." Your stress, your confidence, your consistency or inconsistency all flow straight down to the dog. That is why the Faith Forward K9 Program…
description: Before you train a dog, you train the handler. Lessons from the Faith Forward K9 Program on patience, timing, leadership, and faith.

title: Women Veterans: Seen, Honored, Served
excerpt: March is Women's History Month, a good time to say clearly: women veterans are veterans. Women have served in every American war, as nurses, spies, soldiers in disguise, pilots, and, today, in every branch and nearly…
description: Women veterans are a fast-growing group and often go unseen. Honoring their service and meeting their unique needs, including women experiencing homelessness.

title: Palm Sunday: The King Who Rode a Donkey
excerpt: Conquering generals in the ancient world entered cities on war horses with armies behind them. On Palm Sunday, Jesus entered Jerusalem on a borrowed donkey, with fishermen and ordinary people waving palm branches.…
description: On Palm Sunday Jesus entered Jerusalem on a donkey, not a war horse. What servant leadership looks like for veterans and the Church.

title: Easter: The Unconquered Spirit Rises
excerpt: Christ is risen! He is risen indeed!
description: Christ is risen! Easter is the heart of Faith Forward's motto, Spiritus Invictus, and the ultimate promise that death and despair do not get the last word.

title: Housing First, Faith Always: How Veterans Get Off the Street
excerpt: Across the country, veteran homelessness has dropped significantly since 2010, thanks in large part to targeted programs and a strategy called Housing First. It's one of the clearest proofs that ending homelessness…
description: How veteran housing programs like HUD-VASH and SSVF work, why Housing First matters, and how faith communities complete the picture.

title: Feeding a Working Dog on a Street Budget
excerpt: A healthy dog needs good food, and a good diet doesn't have to cost a fortune. Here's what our K9 program teaches veterans and caregivers. Every dog is different, so check with a veterinarian.
keywords: how much to feed a dog
description: Practical nutrition for veterans' dogs on a tight budget: how much to feed, what to avoid, and how to store food when you live outside.

title: Suicide Prevention: Ask, Care, Escort
excerpt: Too many veterans die by suicide. Every one of them had a name, a story, and people who loved them. You don't need to be a counselor to help. The VA teaches a simple approach called ACE: Ask, Care, Escort.
description: Learn the Ask, Care, Escort approach to veteran suicide prevention. You don't need to be a professional to save a life.

title: Your First Outreach: Volunteering With Faith Forward
excerpt: So you want to serve on the street with us. Thank you! Here's what your first Faith Forward outreach will look like.
description: What to expect on your first Faith Forward outreach: what we carry, how we approach people and dogs, safety, dignity, and prayer.

title: Mental Health Partners: Why We Link, Not Replace
excerpt: May is Mental Health Awareness Month. It's a good time to explain one of Faith Forward's core convictions: we link veterans to licensed mental-health care; we don't replace it.
description: Faith Forward partners with licensed mental-health providers to connect veterans with care. Why faith and clinical care work best together.

title: Mothers Who Serve and Mothers Who Wait
excerpt: Mother's Day can be joyful and painful in the same breath. For military families, it carries layers: the mother deployed overseas missing a child's birthday, the mother at home praying through every news report, and…
description: On Mother's Day, Faith Forward honors mothers who served in uniform, mothers who waited at home, and Gold Star mothers who gave a child to freedom.

title: Armed Forces Day: Honoring Those Who Serve Now
excerpt: Armed Forces Day, held on the third Saturday in May, honors those serving right now in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, and Coast Guard, active, Guard, and Reserve.
description: Armed Forces Day honors those serving today. How to support active-duty service members and why caring for veterans tells them we keep our promises.

title: Heat Is Coming: Summer Safety for Veterans and Their Dogs
excerpt: St. Louis summers bring brutal heat and humidity. For anyone living outside, and for their dogs, heat can be as deadly as winter cold.
description: St. Louis summers are dangerous for people and dogs living outside. Signs of heat illness, hot-pavement tests, cooling centers, and what to donate.

title: Memorial Day: Greater Love Hath No Man
excerpt: Memorial Day is not Veterans Day. Veterans Day thanks the living. Memorial Day honors those who died in service. For many veterans, it's the hardest day of the year: a day of names and faces.
description: Memorial Day honors the men and women who died in military service. A reflection on sacrifice, grief, and how the living can honor the fallen.

title: D-Day Faith: Prayers Before the Storm
excerpt: On June 6, 1944, Allied forces landed on the beaches of Normandy. That night, President Franklin D. Roosevelt went on the radio, not with a speech, but with a prayer, asking the nation to pray with him:
description: On D-Day, President Roosevelt led America in prayer. What the D-Day prayer teaches veterans about facing their own storms with faith.

title: The Army Turns 252: Creeds, Callings, and a Soldier's Faith
excerpt: On June 14, 1775, the Continental Congress established the Continental Army. This June 14, the U.S. Army turns 252, and it's also Flag Day. Happy birthday to every soldier, past and present.
description: On the U.S. Army's 252nd birthday, a reflection on the Soldier's Creed, the Warrior Ethos, and how those words point toward faith.

title: Fathers Who Came Home Different
excerpt: Many veteran fathers came home different. Short tempers. Long silences. Nights out instead of nights home. Some lost their families to the war that followed them home. Many children grew up with a dad who was…
description: For Father's Day, a message for veteran fathers who came home changed, and for their children. Healing, presence, and the Father who never leaves.

title: Fireworks and Flashbacks: Getting Veterans and Dogs Through Loud Nights
excerpt: June 27 is PTSD Awareness Day, and July 4th is next week. For many veterans with combat trauma, and for nearly every dog, the days around the Fourth can mean anxiety, flashbacks, and sleepless nights.
description: Fireworks can trigger veterans with PTSD and terrify dogs. A practical, compassionate guide for neighbors, veterans, and dog owners before July 4th.

title: Freedom Isn't Free, and Neither Is Peace of Mind
excerpt: Happy Independence Day. Today Americans celebrate the freedom declared in 1776 and defended ever since by those who served.
description: On Independence Day, a reflection on the cost of freedom for veterans, the freedom only Christ gives, and how to honor both.

title: Detection Dogs: How a Nose Works Miracles
excerpt: Many veterans served beside detection dogs, and some owe their lives to them. Few things show the genius of God's creation like a dog's nose.
description: How detection dogs find explosives, drugs, and people by scent, how training works, and how veterans and their dogs can enjoy scent work as a sport.

title: Redemption After Incarceration: Justice-Involved Veterans
excerpt: Our founder knows the justice system from the inside. So do many of the veterans we serve. Untreated PTSD, TBI, and substance use can lead veterans into legal trouble, and a record can make housing and jobs much…
description: Many veterans have been involved with the justice system. Veterans Treatment Courts, reentry help, and the faith that no one is beyond redemption.

title: Benefits Claims Without the Runaround: Working With VSOs
excerpt: This week marks the anniversary of the Korean War Armistice (July 27, 1953). Many Korean War veterans waited decades for recognition. Today's veterans shouldn't have to wait that long for benefits they earned.
description: How to file a VA disability claim with free help from accredited Veterans Service Officers, avoid claim sharks, and keep your paperwork straight.

title: A New Mission: Employment After Service
excerpt: In the military, your job was clear and your purpose was obvious. Civilian work can feel like trading a mission for a paycheck. It doesn't have to.
description: Finding meaningful work after the military: translating skills, St. Louis job resources for veterans, and faith that work is a calling.

title: Purple Heart: Wounds, Scars, and Glory
excerpt: August 7 is Purple Heart Day. The Purple Heart, descended from George Washington's Badge of Military Merit, is awarded to those wounded or killed by enemy action. It's one of the most respected decorations in the…
description: On Purple Heart Day, honoring those wounded or killed in combat, and a reflection on the risen Christ who kept His scars.

title: Back to School: Supporting Veteran Families
excerpt: Back-to-school season is a joy for many families and a strain for others. For veteran families facing housing instability or tight budgets, backpacks, supplies, shoes, and clothes add up fast.
description: Back-to-school season strains veteran families on tight budgets. How Faith Forward helps, what to donate, and education benefits veterans' kids can use.

title: Protection Dogs: Power Under Control
excerpt: Many veterans who live outside or in unsafe places want a dog that will protect them. It's understandable. But protection training is serious business, and Faith Forward approaches it honestly.
description: An honest look at protection dog training: what it is, who should do it, breed suitability, the law, and why control matters more than bite.

title: Burn Pits, the PACT Act, and the Care You've Earned
excerpt: Many veterans of Iraq, Afghanistan, and the Gulf lived and worked near burn pits where trash, chemicals, and equipment were burned in the open. Earlier generations faced Agent Orange and other exposures. For years,…
description: The PACT Act expanded VA care and benefits for veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxins. What veterans need to know, and how to get screened.

title: Labor Day: The Dignity of Work
excerpt: Labor Day honors workers and the contributions of labor to our country. Catholic social teaching has a lot to say about work: it has dignity because the worker has dignity, and the economy exists to serve people, not…
description: On Labor Day, a reflection on the dignity of work, Catholic social teaching, and how unemployed and disabled veterans can find purposeful work.

title: Twenty-Six Years After 9/11: The Generation That Answered
excerpt: Twenty-six years ago, on September 11, 2001, nearly 3,000 people were killed in the attacks on New York, Washington, and the plane that crashed in Pennsylvania. Firefighters, police officers, and ordinary people ran…
description: Twenty-six years after September 11, honoring those who died, the first responders, and the post-9/11 generation that answered the call.

title: Suicide Prevention Month: Be There
excerpt: September is Suicide Prevention Month. The VA's message is simple: Be There. Small acts of connection, like a text, a call, a visit, or an invitation, can make a difference for someone who feels alone.
description: September is Suicide Prevention Month. Small acts of connection can save veteran lives. How to be there, and how faith communities can help.

title: St. Michael the Archangel: Patron of Warriors
excerpt: September 29 is the feast of Sts. Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael, Archangels. St. Michael holds a special place for those who serve: he is honored as patron of soldiers, paratroopers, police officers, and first…
description: On the feast of the Archangels, learn why St. Michael is patron of soldiers, police, and first responders, and pray the St. Michael Prayer.

title: St. Francis and the Blessing of the Animals
excerpt: October 4 is the Feast of St. Francis of Assisi, and churches around the world hold a Blessing of the Animals. For Faith Forward, it's one of the most important days of the year.
description: On the Feast of St. Francis, Faith Forward blesses veterans' animals. The story of Francis, creation care, and why every dog deserves a blessing.

title: Building a Foundation That Lasts: Stewardship and Transparency
excerpt: Every gift to Faith Forward, whether a backpack, a bag of dog food, a rosary, or a dollar, is entrusted to us. Paul says the first requirement of a steward is to be faithful. Here's how we work to deserve your trust.
description: How Faith Forward practices stewardship and transparency: governance, accountability, and why donors can trust that every gift goes to its purpose.

title: One Year of Faith Forward: What God Has Done
excerpt: When Samuel's people won a hard-fought victory, he set up a stone and named it Ebenezer: "Hitherto hath the LORD helped us." As Faith Forward approaches one year, we're setting up our own Ebenezer.
description: Looking back on the first year of Faith Forward Foundation: veterans served, dogs helped, lessons learned, and gratitude to everyone who made it possible.

title: Faith Forward: The Mission Continues
excerpt: Our name says it: Faith Forward. Not faith frozen in the past, but faith moving forward. As we close our first year of weekly articles and head toward another Veterans Day, here's where we're going.
description: Faith Forward's vision for the year ahead: growing outreach, training trainers, expanding the K9 program, and inviting St. Louis to join the mission.
